escalations.question: MASTER-164's prescribed remedy (convert ExpandToggle from Label to transparent glyph Button) was declined by the user at sub-session 5c's escalation E5 because the siblings render 55x55 against the Label's 16x23, changing header-row height. Re-decide it, now that measurement shows the 55x55 is WinUI's default Button minimum rather than a chosen size and can be overridden.
escalations.answer: Resolved by the documentation research round the user requested. The focusable-card-body option is NOT VIABLE: IsTabStop, TabIndex and ITabStopElement are absent from .NET MAUI 10's public API, and MAUI 9 deliberately removed layout focus (its own what's-new example is a VerticalStackLayout whose Focus handler 'isn't executed because only input controls can gain focus'); at the platform layer a Border/Grid/StackPanel is not a WinUI Control and so supports neither focus nor tab navigation. The remedy is therefore the transparent glyph Button, which is what Microsoft's keyboard-accessibility guidance explicitly prescribes for this exact anti-pattern and which needs no platform code, satisfying both of the user's stated priorities. The header-height objection that caused the 5c E5 decline is resolvable: keep the ~16x23 visual and pad the hit area to >=23x23, which Microsoft's touch guidance sanctions for a progressive-disclosure control whose function is redundant with another target. Two things documentation could not settle and which the implementing task must verify by running: whether MinimumWidthRequest/MinimumHeightRequest override the WinUI default Button minimum, and whether the header row height changes.

escalations.question: What instrument verifies MASTER-163 and MASTER-164 against the running application? src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests is an existing Appium harness proven 2026-09-04 that drives the real unpackaged exe, but it is deliberately outside src/DungeonMaster.sln and needs an Appium server plus Developer Mode.
escalations.answer: Extend the existing Appium harness in src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests. The floor-sidebar facts become repeatable tests that survive the session and guard the fix, accepting the Appium-server and Developer-Mode prerequisites the project's README already documents. Constrained at Gate 2 by the measured finding that synthetic input cannot drive native WinUI drag-and-drop and that Appium's ability to do so is unproven: T5 carries an explicit fallback rather than a criterion resting on that instrument.

escalations.question: The cursor claims behind MASTER-161 and MASTER-165 cannot be settled by any automated instrument or by the orchestrator driving the app. HandCursorBehavior sets WinUI's non-public ProtectedCursor, which another process cannot read, and the repository already records that a GetCursorInfo probe measures the apparatus rather than the change. Cursor claims need a human observer.
escalations.answer: Ran a discriminating probe with all three attach configurations observable in a single launch, varied by floor number. The user observed the hand cursor on ALL THREE configurations including the untouched as-shipped one. MASTER-161's remedy therefore works and the entry closes done; MASTER-165's claim is falsified. The surviving half of the original 2026-09-01 observation is AreaSidebarItem's card body, which carries no HandCursorBehavior at all - absence, not inertness - and was scoped into T3 at Gate 2 as MASTER-175.

escalations.question: MASTER-166's suspected mechanism needs frame-complete capture to settle; the original 60ms burst is roughly 4x too slow to sample a single-frame event. A candidate remedy (move ClearGhostAreas after RefreshFloorAsync) is justifiable independently of settling the observation, because it also closes a window in which neither the ghost nor the persisted area exists.
escalations.answer: Instrument and settle the mechanism by measurement rather than by frame capture: establish whether the awaited AddAreaWithOutline write returns inside one frame interval, which decides whether the ghost is structurally unreachable at local-database latency. The remedy follows from that measurement instead of preceding it. Assigned to T4, whose criteria forbid overstating a consistent observation as a proven cause.

escalations.question: Three acceptance criteria (T1 c3, T2 c6, T3 c5) are met only by a person looking at the running application. The owning task cannot execute them, and dir-reviewer judges against the criteria and nothing else. Who executes them, and how does the reviewer reach the evidence?
escalations.answer: The orchestrator runs each observation with the user when its task reports done, and hands the observation transcript to dir-reviewer alongside the diff. The task's deliverable is the observation protocol, stated precisely enough to be executed unchanged. Absent a transcript the criterion is UNDETERMINED rather than met, so a missing observation cannot be silently scored as a pass. The alternative of folding all three into one post-T3 session was rejected because it would serialize the reviews on top of an already-serial task chain.

options.summary: Orchestrator runs each observation when its task reports done and hands the transcript to the reviewer
options.rationale: Keeps the serial chain moving and gives the reviewer reachable evidence for a criterion its own rules would otherwise leave unjudgeable.

options.summary: Fold all three observations into one session after T3 lands
options.rationale: One app launch instead of three, but T1's and T2's reviews then block on T3, serializing the reviews as well as the tasks.

options.summary: Downgrade all three to advisory and let the structural criteria carry the tasks
options.rationale: Cheapest and wrong: the reorder defect is only observable, and T3's finding came from a human in the first place.

escalations.question: T1's premise is void. The controlled observation shows the floor reorder works end to end - UI and database agree, Guest Rooms moved 3->7 and persisted. The failure recorded in measurement.md was taken in a scrolling, non-maximized window with the overlay scrollbar rendered; this run had no scrollbar. So the 'new unrecorded functional defect' is a symptom of MASTER-163 (a drop that misses every drop target is discarded silently - FloorListContainer has no DropGestureRecognizer), not a peer defect. manifest.json is frozen and MASTER-163's severity was to be corrected DOWNWARD by T6; the observation argues it should go UP, and MASTER-174's characterisation is now wrong.
escalations.answer: Amend. MASTER-163 becomes the session's primary defect and its severity is corrected UPWARD, not downward: when a drop misses every drop target the operation fails silently with no error and no feedback, which is why the feature reads as broken. T3 gains a criterion that a missed drop no longer fails silently - either FloorListContainer accepts drops, or the miss is surfaced. T6's instruction flips accordingly, and MASTER-174 is filed as 'a drop that misses every drop target is discarded silently' rather than 'the reorder does not reorder', which is false. T1's work stands: a behaviour-preserving refactor plus the first tests on the gesture-to-command path, and it correctly declined to ship a speculative fix. Separately: the user chose to leave Test Dungeon #1 with Guest Rooms at position 7 rather than restore it.

escalations.question: T2 shipped the expand toggle at 44x44 rather than contract C3 section 1's pinned ~23x23, because MinimumWidthRequest="23" is a bare literal that fails GeometryScaleTests.NoBareGeometryValues, and the legal remedy - a token in Resources/Theme/Tokens.xaml - lives in a file T2 does not own.
escalations.answer: Keep 44x44 as shipped. It matches the three sibling Buttons in the same header row exactly, clears the touch-target minimum outright rather than relying on the progressive-disclosure redundancy carve-out, and introduces no new theme token. Accepted cost is horizontal only: chevron column 13 -> 44, floor-name label 160 -> 129. Height unchanged, which is the invariant that mattered. Declined: adding a DmDisclosureTargetMinimum token to pin 29x27, and recording the file in MinimumSizePendingMigration - the latter would degrade a ratchet that documents undecided legacy cases by using it to wave through a deliberate new value.

options.rationale: Matches the three sibling Buttons in the same row, clears the touch minimum outright, needs no new token.

options.summary: Add a DmDisclosureTargetMinimum token and pin 29x27
options.rationale: Closest to the contract's stated intent and keeps 15px more room for floor names, but needs an owner for Tokens.xaml.
Cheapest, and recommended against by both T2 and the orchestrator: that census documents undecided legacy cases, not exemptions for deliberate new values.

escalations.question: c7 cannot be satisfied from T3's owns set. The criterion asserts DungeonDetailPage.xaml being owned means no ownership change is needed, but XAML event handlers resolve against DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs, which is T4's file; and the command-bound route needs DungeonDetailViewModel, owned by nobody. Both acceptable shapes therefore require a file T3 does not own.
escalations.answer: Grant T3 src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs and src/DungeonMaster.App.Core/Editor/FloorReorder*.cs, and re-dispatch T3 for c7 alone. The orchestrator verified this creates no unordered ownership intersection: T4 already depends on T3 and T3 already depends on T1, so both new overlaps carry a direct dependsOn edge, and neither task is running. Keeps the fix attached to the task whose report and contract amendment describe it. T3 recommends shape (a) - FloorListContainer accepts drops - on the evidence that the drag placeholder already previews where the floor will land, so a release on that gap is an expressed intention rather than a meaningless drop.

options.summary: Grant T3 the two files and re-dispatch for c7 alone
options.rationale: No unordered intersection is created and neither task is running; keeps the fix with the task that documented it.
T4 already owns DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs and runs next, but its criteria say nothing about the silent discard and it is the ghost-frame measurement task.

options.summary: Leave c7 unmet and file the silent discard for a later session
options.rationale: Honest but leaves E6's finding unremedied and records 'nothing happens' at the observation a second time.

escalations.question: T3 reports a discipline conflict it did not escalate as blocking: the frontend discipline requires every interactive element be reachable and operable by keyboard alone, and floor reordering is pointer-only - OnKeyDown at DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:361-430 has no reorder key, as contract C1 section 3 records. T3's task is layout-only and the contract freezes the gesture host, so it did not act.
escalations.answer: File it as a new numbered audit entry, MASTER-176, carrying T3's evidence. It is a genuine accessibility gap and a discipline-conformance failure, not merely a nicety: MASTER-164 restored keyboard access to a floor's areas this session, which makes reorder the remaining pointer-only operation in the sidebar. Filed this session, not fixed.
